title: The Underground Choir of Locked Substations

features.name: locked transformer cabinet
features.desc-on-touch: Behind the rusted padlock, you hear the hum. It is a single note that has not stopped singing for decades. The cabinet is marked with dates of lock-ins—1987, 1994, 2003, 2015. No one has opened it since.

features.name: the resonance ground
features.desc-on-touch: The earth itself vibrates at the frequency. You feel it through your feet—a slow tremor that has been singing for so long the ground has learned the melody.

features.name: the singing cables
features.desc-on-touch: Barely visible in the dark—cables running from the cabinet into the earth, vibrating so faintly you might imagine it. But the hum comes from them, you realize. The cables have learned to sing.

inscription: the choir will not need the key; it is learning to sing louder than the lock

file.name: Substation_Frequency_Log_1982-Present.txt
file.note: Forty years of harmonic readings from three buried substations. When graphed by date, the frequency rises one hertz per year, as if the electricity were learning a song.
